newsitem.title: USA: Enron submits documents to Ore. commission.
newsitem.headline: Enron submits documents to Ore. commission.

text.p: Enron Corp and Portland General Corp on Friday submitted additional materials to staff of the Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC), clearing the way for a meeting on Tuesday, the OPUC said.
Tom Riordan, senior analyst at the state commission, said the documents are under review, but cannot be commented on until after next week's settlement meeting.

The meeting was called by the three-member OPUC a week ago at a special hearing convened to clarify the regulatory agency's expectations from the planned merger of Enron and Portland General Electric.

A previous settlement conference failed with staff of the OPUC making approval of the merger conditional on a $47.4 million annual rate cut, compared with the companies' estimate of $3 million annually in merger-related savings.
Enron chairman Kenneth Lay said last week final approval of the merger by OPUC clearly would require the identification of more savings for Oregon customers.
